Stocks are set to become scarcer as mine production continues to disappoint, with Chilean and Peruvian production down by 4% and 5% respectively in January despite new projects coming on stream. Exchange stocks have been on a declining trend for the past two years, as the chart to the right shows. However, over the past few months there has been a sharp divergence between regions. LME stocks in Asia and Europe have been all but depleted and US stocks held on the exchange continue their rapid decline that started in December. On the SHFE, though, stocks rose to a 10-year high of 227,276t on 16th March. The other significant stocks available to the global copper market are those in Shanghai bonded warehouses. When our estimates of 575,000t are added to exchange inventories the total for material that is readily available doubles to over 1Mt. However, this is still below the almost 1.25Mt reached in March last year. Chinese stocks rise, as in 2011,

Bonded warehouse stocks in China follow a pronounced seasonal pattern, as Chinese copper traders store their working inventory in them. By doing so they postpone paying VAT on the metal and leave themselves the option of re-exporting the cathode if market conditions change and prices outside the country become more attractive. With the arbitrage significantly negative, we are hearing that when reported March export figures should be higher. Bonded stocks

hit their nadir in November last year at 200,000t and have been rising since, accelerating in January and February to almost 600,000t.  On the face of it, this repeats the pattern of 2011. However, the owners of these stocks are different from last year. 

### …with traders appearing to drive them up this year 

Of this bonded material, 200,000-300,000t is generally considered to account for the working inventory of Chinese copper traders.  Last year, the rise in bonded stocks to almost 600,000t was driven by property speculators using copper as a financing mechanism to overcome the tight credit conditions.  That activity appears to have been stamped out as part of the deflation of the property bubble in China.  This year, the driver of the rise seems to be traders.  We believe that some of the rise is the usual increase in Q1 of working inventory by traders ahead of increased seasonal demand following the Chinese Spring Festival. However, on top of this, some traders may be using copper as a financing mechanism to take advantage of arbitrage opportunities in other markets, such as in the RMB and interest rates.  We have heard from traders selling into China that many of the sales into the country lately have been to large traders, which is consistent with this explanation.  However, the negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME prices has risen from a monthly average of around $40/t to $326/t in February and

$370/t in the month to 26<sup>th</sup> March.  The March figure represents an almost 5% loss on metal if it were sold in China, which should restrain traders from ramping bonded stocks ever higher.  As it turns out, we have heard recently that the rate of increase in bonded stocks has slowed, though it does remain remains on an upward trend. 

### Chinese imports stay up despite anaemic consumption 

The level of imports of copper and other raw materials into China remained at near record levels in February, as can be seen in the chart at the right.  The rebound of refined imports to over 375,000t 000t Cu in February from the holiday affected decline in January fuelled the 800 rise in bonded warehouse stocks noted earlier.  This continued 700 strength in imports of copper in all its forms is a surprising result, 600 given that copper consumption growth has been anaemic following 500 the Spring Festival in January.  There has been a seasonal increase 400 in consumption, but it has just not been as strong as many expected. The lingering effect of the Chinese Central Bank’s credit squeeze to 300 deflate the property price bubble means that copper semi-fabricators 200 are still finding it difficult to secure credit.  In addition, end users of 100 copper semis are facing high levels of inventory of final goods that 0 will need to be sold before they place significant new orders for Jan-07 copper semis.  As a result, semi-fabricators

themselves are facing reduced utilisation rates and a build in inventories of semi-fabricated products. Blister & Anode

The slowdown in demand for cathode has seen further downward pressure on premia for imported cathode, which fell to $30-70/t in March. We noted a slight increase in cathode inventory at semi-fabricators earlier in Q1 in anticipation of the stronger seasonal demand. However, the abundance of cathode means there could be some modest de-stocking in the short term. The large negative arbitrage between SHFE and the LME is also restraining imports of scrap, which in January and February combined fell by 3% y-o-y. This compares to concentrates imports rising by 27% y-o-y in the same two months. This is in part to replenish the rundown of concentrate inventory that took place last year, as well as to compensate for lower imported scrap availability. The increase in concentrates imports is supporting strong growth in refined production in China, which rose by 17% in the first two months of 2012. As a result of the increased production, mediocre consumption, high bonded stocks and low premia, we expect to see a decline in the figures for Chinese cathode imports for March. ### US LME stocks decline sharply… The US is another area where stock movements are impacting the market. The high levels of US cancelled warrants are generating many theories among market participants to explain them. in the warehouses and the lots for which the warrant has been cancelled. This is the tonnage that is actually available to the market. The massive decline began in December in New Orleans. This could be associated with a movement of metal to China to take advantage of the then positive SHFE/LME arbitrage. The LME warehouse stocks in Asia had been depleted, as had already low European stocks, leaving the US the only source of LME stocks. However, trade data shows that only about 3,000t was shipped to China out of the US in January, which is a far cry from the 14,625t withdrawn from New Orleans between 23rd December and 24th January. So China is unlikely to be the main

reason for the drop.  With the arbitrage window firmly shut since January, it is difficult to believe that the warrants cancelled since then will go to China either. 

Over the past couple of years, US consumption had to be met by Data: LME drawing on stocks in LME warehouses to fill a gap in supply.  This was clearly seen in the steady drawdown in New Orleans stocks from early 2010 to late 2011 (offset only marginally by rising stocks in other locations as shown in the chart).  The slowdown in US economic growth and copper consumption in H2 2011 reduced the need for LME stocks, with the total rising between July and December. 

The recent improvement in sentiment about US economic prospects, driven especially by better employment figures, could lead to higher copper consumption and a resumption of draw downs in LME stocks to meet demand.  However, this is not yet evident in US spot cathode purchases.  Spot deals remained few and far between in March.  It is too early to say with conviction that there has actually been an increase in consumption and, if so, whether or not this is being met through annual contract material instead of spot metal.  As a result of the low level of spot activity, premia have remained roughly the same as last month at 5.75-6.25¢/lb, supported by high gasoline prices that are boosting the freight element. 

### …consumption, warehouse war or disappearing act? 

Given the limited load out rates from LME warehouses of 1,500t/d, the large number of cancelled warrants in New Orleans has created a queue.  As New Orleans open tonnage bottomed out, open tonnage in St Louis began to decline, most likely due to a decline in availability of freely available warrants in New Orleans.  This rate of decline mirrored that of New Orleans, but may have been due to a band wagon effect.  Traders who have come to rely on LME warehouses for copper may have panicked a bit.  Once they saw that St Louis warrants were being cancelled, they may have jumped in to secure tonnages for their use later in the Spring to meet seasonally stronger demand.  At the same time that the queue began to lengthen in St Louis, the chart above shows that open tonnage began to fall in Chicago.  However, the Chicago decline was more gradual and from a lower level.  This more gradual descent appears more consistent with the withdrawals being to meet consumption.  This view is further supported by the recent increase in cancelled warrants at COMEX 

© 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** 

Page 4 of 18 

Copper Monitor 

April 2012 

www. crugroup.com 

warehouses.  These have risen to around 12,000t and the arbitrage between LME cash and 1<sup>st</sup> position COMEX has narrowed almost to parity from COMEX being 2.5¢/lb higher on average in February. 

The Chicago data also illustrates clearly the impact of warehouse competition.  In the three circled sections, warrants were cancelled in one LME warehouse, withdrawn and then put into another warehouse in the

same location. This could have been due to either a better storage deal being offered to a warrant holder or to a consolidation of warrant holdings by the parent company owner of a warehouse. The larger drawdowns in New Orleans and St Louis stocks have not yet demonstrated a similar pattern, suggesting that these movements are unlikely to be due to warehouse competition. The decline in New Orleans stocks seems to have triggered this wider fall in US exchange stocks. With neither consumption nor exports sufficient reasons, there is another possibility. Someone may have taken the metal out of the LME system to help foster an impression of physical tightness. A flat forward curve, to hedge the price downside, and cheap financing mean a player could be betting on the deficit forecast for 2012 coming true. If it does, prices and premia should rise and they would profit handsomely. ### European consumption outlook less gloomy In Europe, the LTRO (Long Term Refinancing Operation) three year loan programme by the European Central Bank means that the sovereign debt crisis will not immediately translate into a banking crisis. This has lightened the outlook somewhat for Europe. We still expect consumption to decline this year, as the Eurozone goes into recession. However, a catastrophic collapse seems to have been averted, at least until the LTRO expires. Spot demand for cathode was supported by the delay to some imported material earlier in the month. Low levels of both LME stocks in the region and annual contract volumes have meant that this quickly translated into higher premia. Those on material for delivery to a Northwest European port jumped to over $100/t, but in the past two weeks this fell back to $80-100/t. With concerns over rising Spanish bond yields showing the crisis is not solved, European debt problems will continue to weigh on the copper market. ### Price to remain range bound Copper prices have been on a rising trend since the collapse to below $7,000/t in October last year. This has raised the 30-day moving average above the 200-day average, signalling technical strength as seen in the chart to the right. The upward momentum has stalled, with prices trading in a tight band of $8,200-8,600/t since January However, the down side is limited by a solid floor under the price due to low stock levels and struggling mine production. As noted last month, investors have cautiously moved back into copper. The US outlook seems to be improving, but until uncertainties about Chinese consumption and Eurozone debt are reduced, we expect investors to remain cautious and the copper price to continue to trade sideways. Some differences in the quarterly trend pattern of demand for flat rolled products are in evidence when observing the data by raw material. Alloyed copper flat rolled products enjoyed significantly better growth in H1 over its pure copper counterpart, but then underperformed in the latter half of the year. We attribute this pattern to the copper price, which was at a sustained high level for much of H1, encouraging substitution of use for cheaper brass flat rolled products. However, the substitution effect reversed in late Q3 and Q4 as copper became more affordable for use in flat rolled products. The regional split of copper and copper alloy PSSF production indicates that all the major regions exhibited a seasonal rise in Q2, followed by a downturn in Q3 and Q4. Macroeconomic events impinged on demand, impacting order levels and production. In China, this mainly involved the tightening of credit availability due to the government’s attempts to tackle high inflation rates. This led to downstream user destocking and piecemeal copper and alloy flat rolled product ordering strategies. Since demand in China, accounting for 61% of Cu PSSF and 73% of Cu AL PSSF regional totals, outweighs domestic production in China, accounting for 53% and 65% respectively, China is therefore dependent upon its neighbouring countries for an adequate supply of flat rolled products. Another primarily European copper and copper alloys semis fabricator, **KME Group** , reported a contraction of copper, alloy and special products output of 10.5% y-o-y in Q4 2011.  The company attributed the weak performance to a slowdown in the construction sector, which is the main end-use sector for 25-30% of the group’s product range.  Additionally, KME cited the copper price volatility, economic uncertainty and difficulty in securing bank financing as factors that encouraged customers to de-stock through the period. 

Automotive Sector Growth 2011 y-o-y change in output of light vehicle units 

The Americas also encountered a difficult economic environment in 2011.  A sustained downturn in the US real estate sector, which had not begun to recover from the global economic crisis in 2008/09, as well as concerns about employment levels and fiscal policy in the US caused consumers of copper and alloy flat rolled products, concerned over demand prospects, to delay or downsize their orders. **Olin Brass** , a copper and copper alloy flat rolled product fabricator and subsidiary of **Global Brass,** reported poor trading conditions in t

he first nine months of 2011, as the company saw a decline in sales volumes of 15% y-o-y or -36.2Mlbs, which it attributed to macroeconomic factors, industry overcapacity and copper price volatility.  Specifically, housing overcapacity and a decrease in consumer spending had been depressing the building and housing, automotive and coinage sectors (accounting for 23% of sales by metal weight in 2010), however, the munitions sector, representing 43% of shipments by volume in 2010, was still

supportive of demand.  The bankruptcy of **Hussey Copper Ltd.** in late Q3 remedied some of the overcapacity issues affecting the US flat rolled copper products industry.  Aurubis said that delivery volumes from its facility in **Buffalo, NY** expanded by 15% y-o-y.  However, we understand that overall underlying demand had not improved vastly and customers elected to accelerate orders ahead of Christmas earlier than usual, leading to more destocking activity in Q4 2011 than the previous year.  We estimate that US Q4 production of Cu PSSF was 26,000t and Cu AL PSSF was 54,200t, down by 1.6% and 8.2% y-o-y, respectively.  South and Central American production of copper and copper alloy PSSF rose by 4.2% y-o-y to total around 70,000t in 2011.  This was mainly due to the positive swing in Brazil’s net trade in H1 2011, indicating an increased level of competitiveness of domestic production against imports.  However, Brazil’s flat rolled copper market returned to trade deficit from July as the Real appreciated rapidly, effectively tempering the full year production growth rate seen in South and Central America. 

### Q4 flat rolled product consumer performances 

An important first use for copper and copper alloy flat rolled products is in the manufacture of connectors, which in turn have a diverse mix of uses in the automotive, industrial, communication and information technology, consumer electronics, military and medical sectors. **Molex** and **Amphenol** are two large global players in this industry with Q4 2011 revenues of US$858M and US$902M, respectively. 

In its Q4 results, Molex reported that it received many of its usual Christmas order bookings in September as customers sought cheap freight and were wary of demand uncertainty given the delicate macroeconomic environment in many regions in late 2011.  All sectors therefore performed weakly sequentially from Q3.  The **Telecoms sector** (accounting for 26% of company revenue) was amongst the most resilient sectors in terms of demand, as orders dropped only 5% driven by the strong smartphone market.  Orders from the **Industrial sector** (accounting for 13% of company revenue) fell by 4%, supported by auto customers looking to retool operations in North America but weakened by distributor destocking and end-users delaying automation projects and capacity expansions due to the economic conditio

ns. The **Consumer Electronics** and **Infotech** markets (accounting for 18% and 24% of company revenue) registered sequential declines in demand of 15% and 17% q-o-q. These sectors were both indirectly impacted by the flooding in Thailand but also by low production volumes attributed to the weak economic climate and accelerated pre-Christmas stock-builds. Orders from the **Automotive sector** , which accounts for 16% of Molex’s sales, fell by 10% in Q4 2011, supported by domestic auto demand particularly in North America, but let-down by weaker production levels in France and Southern Europe in Q4. Amphenol announced a similar pattern of results, registering sequential declines in revenues in the consumer driven **Mobile devices** and **Communication technology** sectors of 17% and 7% q-o-q in Q4. - **Superior Essex Energy Inc.** , the US based energy cablemaking division of Superior Essex Inc., began commercial production of its new suite of low voltage energy cables, it was announced on February 28<sup>th</sup> .  The new products include 300V and 600V instrumentation cables and 600V control cables for industrial, utility power or station control circuits.  The company is manufacturing its new offering out of its Tarboro, NC facility which represents Superior Essex Inc.'s first North American production facility for low voltage energy cables. 

- **The Chinese Association of Automobile Manufactures** reported Chinese automobile production at 2.9M units, down by 4.9% y-o-y in Jan-Feb 2012.  February output levels increased by 23.8% m-o-m to reach 1.6M units following the January new year holiday. 

- German company **Kromberg & Shubert** has launched the construction of a €20M (US$26.1M) car cables plant in south-western Macedonia.  The construction works, which are performed by Turkish company **Pera Construction** , are expected to be completed by the end of the year.  The plant is located in the Zabeni free industrial zone, near the city of Bitola, and is expected to employ over 2,500 people.  Kromberg & Shubert manufactures on-board networks, cables, plastic technology and mechatronics. 

- On 7<sup>th</sup> March, it was reported that the **Rio de Janeiro State Government** has introduced a tax incentive plan to initiate and promote the growth of the downstream copper industry.  A reduction in the VAT on copper products from 19% to 2% has already led to a decision by **Ibrame** , the Brazilian manufacturer of copper cathode, wirerod and bar, to construct a copper rod mill in **Itatiaia** .  Upon commissioning in early 2013 the facility is initially expected to produce 70,000t/y of wirerod, processed mainly from direct-use scrap, with capacity rising to 100,000t/y in subsequent years.

- It was announced on 22<sup>nd</sup> March that **Nexans** will be the first major tenant in a business park near Goose Creek, outside Charleston, S.C.  The new $85 million plant will employ 200 people and construction is expected to start this year with hiring beginning in late 2013. 

- It was reported that the value of output at **Canghuan Copper Products Co. Ltd.** Reached RMB2.9B in 2011.  This represents growth of 32% y-o-y.  The company, which is owned by the Golden Dragon Group, produces high precision tubes for air conditioning, oxygen-free copper tubes for the solar power sector, as well as microelectronic components anf radio-frequency cables.  In January Canghuan Copper began an expansion project which will increase its production capacity from 5,000t/y to 100,000t/y. 

### Mi

ne Production 

- **Freeport-McMoRan** resumed operations at its **Grasberg** mine on 12<sup>th</sup> March after reaching an agreement with the workers’ union.  Operations at the mine were suspended on 23rd February amid security concerns and unresolved issues between the management and the workers.  This disruption comes after workers returned to work in January following a three-month long strike at the mine that caused an estimated production loss of 115,000t of contained copper.  We currently expect Grasberg to produce 464,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2012. 

- On 21<sup>st</sup> February, the **Indonesian President** signed a new mining regulation into law that limits foreign ownership of Indonesian mining operations to 49%.  The new law says that foreign mining operations must gradually divest a minimum of 51% of ownership to Indonesian entities within a 10 year period.  It is believed that currently operating mines will not be affected until their mining licences are due for renewal. 

- On 22nd March, the mines minister of the **Democratic Republic of Congo** announced that he intends to introduce changes to the country’s ‘outdated’ mining code.  The exact details of the proposed changes are not yet available.  However, the minister stated that he plans to raise taxes paid by mining companies and to increase the 5% minimum automatic stake that the state receives in new mine projects.  Last year, the DR Congo’s government reportedly raised around US$100M in mining taxes. 

- On 16<sup>th</sup> March, it was reported that the talks over a new labour contract between the management and workers **at First Quantum Minerals** ’ **Kansanshi** mine in Zambia had collapsed and were set to be resolved in an industrial relations court.  On March 4th, the management and the workers agreed to a 15% pay rise, however, the dispute is continuing over the permanence and duration of the workers’ contracts.  This comes after the workers staged a five-day strike at the mine from the 1<sup>st</sup> -6<sup>th</sup> March, causing production at the mine to grind to a halt.  This is the second strike at the mine this year. In 2012, the mine is expected to produce 144,000t of copper-inconcentrate.

- On 1<sup>st</sup> March, the **Zambian Environmental Management Agency** (ZEMA) ordered **Glencore** ’s **Mopani Copper Mines** to shut down its **Mufulira** heap leaching plant due to pollution violations.  The agency suspects that the emissions of acid mist have caused an increase in pulmonary, throat, nose and ear ailments in the surrounding area.  Mopani copper mines subsequently announced that it will spend US$145M on an anti-pollution programme over the next two years.  The Mopani Copper mines heap leaching plant is expected to produce 6,000t of EW cathode in 2012. 

- Heavy rains in Northern Chile have continued to affect the operations of se

veral major mines in the area.  On 13<sup>th</sup> March, it was reported that the **Haldeman Mining Company** , owners of the **Sagasca** mine, had declared force majeure, following mudslides disrupting operations. Furthermore, access roads to the **Collahuasi** and **Cerro Colorado** mines became impassable due to flooding and there have been unconfirmed reports of direct flooding on the grounds of the Collahuasi mine itself.  Nevertheless, it was reported that operations have continued. 

- In an auction held on 26th March, Romanian state-owned mining company, **Cupru Min SA Abrud** , was sold to Canada’s **Roman Copper Corporation** for €200.8M (US$266M).  Cupru Min Abrud’s main line of business is the operation of the **Roşia Poieni** deposit, one of the largest copper deposits in Europe, estimated to contain copper reserves of 900,000t. 

- Central Chile was hit by a 7.1 magnitude earthquake on 25<sup>th</sup> March.  However, no casualties were reported and there was no serious damage to infrastructure.  There are several major copper mines near the epicentre of the earthquake, including **Codelcos** ’s **Andina** and **El Teniente** and Anglo **American** ’s **Los Bronces** .  However, operations at the mines were reported to be normal. This is the largest earthquake to hit Chile, since the 8.8 magnitude tremor in 2010 that caused 500 fatalities and major destruction. 

### Exploration and Development 

- In a statement by **Codelco** on 6<sup>th</sup> March, the company announced plans to invest US$4.33B in its Chilean mines in 2012.  This is a substantial increase from the US$2.5B the company spent in 2011. This is part of a strategy to counteract the declining output levels and boost output to 2.1Mt of copper by 2020. 

- On March 21<sup>st</sup> , it was reported that **Ivanhoe Mines** , majority owned by **Rio Tinto** , is facing problems in securing power supply for its **Oyu Tolgoi** project in Mongolia.  The original plan was for the mine to be connected to the Chinese power grid, across the border.  However, this may need to be revised as an agreement between China and Mongolia had still not been reached. This can potentially cause serious delays in the original production schedule.  The Oyu Tolgoi project is planned to start up in 6 months, and is expected to produce up to 610,000t/y of copperin-concentrate at its peak.

### Smelting and Refining 

- **Pan Pacific Copper** is reported to be experiencing production problems at the **Tamano** smelter (operated by **Hibi Kyodo** ).  According to reports, a malfunctioning boiler caused the smelter to shut down from the 6th-21st February. 

- On 20<sup>th</sup> March, the management of **Glencore** ’s **PASAR** smelter in the Philippines announced that the smelter is expected to resume operations in June or July.  This comes after operations were halted in January followi

ng a fire.  PASAR’s spokesman explained that the fire had damaged the anti-pollution devices (i.e. the sulphuric acid plant) at the smelter and new equipment had been ordered from China. 

- On 19<sup>th</sup> March, it was reported that **Codelco** had restarted the **Chuquicamata** smelter in Northern Chile after production had been halted for a month due to a blocked chimney.  The smelter is expected to produce 360,000t copper-in-blister in 2012. 

- On 26<sup>th</sup> March, it was announced that Tanzania’s first copper smelter operated by **Danformation** is due to start operations within a few days with the arrival of first consignment of ore.  The smelter has already been commissioned and currently has a capacity of 12,00018,000t/y of copper-in-blister that will gradually be expanded to 240,000t/y.  This is the first of six smelters that Danformation plans to build in Tanzania.
